instruction.text: Drag the London attack to the gap in the timeline of Viking raids on Britain.

atoms.b: In AD 850, the Vikings travelled down the River Thames and attacked ((++London America)).
Unlike previous attacks, the Anglo-Saxons could not completely get rid of the ((++Vikings English)). Instead, the Vikings spent the winter camped outside the city.

instruction.text: What does this outcome tell us about the Vikings?

feedback.end: This is the Viking leader Ragnar Lodbrok. He led many raids across the coasts of England and France.

instruction.text: According to legend, Ragnar was killed when the Anglo-Saxons threw him in a pit of snakes. Find the snakes to hear what he said before he died.

atoms.sound: How the little piglets would grunt if they knew how the boar suffered.

atoms.a: When Ragnar talks about “the boar”, who do you think he is referring to?
Who are the little piglets that Ragnar is referring to?
What do you think Ragnar is saying here?
b: ++the Vikings will want to get revenge
the Vikings will be happy he died

instruction.text: Do you think Ragnar really said this?

feedback.end: It is unlikely that this actually happened — especially the part about the snakes! However, the story of his death still inspired his people to take action...
